questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always been drawn to Italy; the history, food, art, architecture and literature. I have always admired Umberto Eco who lived in Milan, and loved the stories of Italo Calvino that also have connections to Milan. Furthermore, the Italian academy has a rich tradition, different from the Danish - another reason for visiting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite hard. University websites are notoriously difficult to navigate, and Unimi's is no different. There was perhaps a lack of communication from both UCPH and Unimi in the early days of the stay, where insecurity is high.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved an e-mail maybe 10 days after arrival on where to collect my student card, but this e-mail conflicted with information on the uni-website.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was clear that there would be a lot of administrative work on my own hand, which I of course did not enjoy too much. However, when I sought help, everyone was generous with their assistance.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Hmm, slightly difficult. It is important to begin early. Housing in Milan is super expensive. AirBnB is a good place to start.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Prioritise living close to uni! I did, and it was wonderful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Milan is expensive, but it is still on the "cheaper" Erasmus scholarship tier. So just know that it can be expensive, depending on where you are looking.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was not too difficult - my challenges arose specifically because of difficulties with my pre-approval. It was hard finding courses that met the requirements made by UCPH.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First I had to enroll in the uni erasmus portal. This was easy. Later on, once I had gotten my email-credentials, I had to register for courses, which was a bit more difficult, since there were troubles with the pre-approval (and also not always reading lists available for the Unimi-courses).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Lots of help was available, just not very easily. There wasn't a desk where you could show up to get help. Emailing the professors and coordinators was probably the best way to get help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I took me maybe 10 attempts to get to the right courses, in part due to last-minute re-scheduling of one of my courses. Once I had found the four courses I needed though, everything was great.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look through the course catalogue and send out mails VERY early. Be persistent (maybe even annoying), university-bureaucracy is stubborn and slow (this was my experience in both Copenhagen and Milan). If possible, try and make some calls, so that you can get immediate answers.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Fantastic courses, all four that I attended. However, there were not enough readings in my opinion. This was more prevalent in some courses. In one course, we were 70 students enrolled, and only a 30-pers-classroom. To me, there was a lack of common ground, since we were so many international students, which could be fixed by having more readings to create a point of departure of deliberations.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As mentioned above, there was a lack of readings in most courses - however there was also room for personal effort.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is more of a historical and an oral tradition in Milan. 4/5 exams were oral - in Copenhagen I haven't had one yet, and wont have one for at least a year. It was very nice developing my on-the-spot-arguing-skills and rhetorics. I nice and welcome change.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
History of Regional Integrations (6 ects)
Journalism, Media and Politics (9 ects)
Comparative Legal Traditions (6 ects)
Comparative Politics and Development (9 ects)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would honestly recommend all the courses, they were fantastic. The professors were very kind and skilled, and the objectives of the courses aligned with all of my interests, and adressed challenges of crucial importance. With regards to the Journalism, Media and Politics course, be sure to ask for some readings - and try to lobby for a larger classroom.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The deposit for the apartment was expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Living was very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not engage too much in the erasmus activities, probably because I was still in a covid mindset. It took some time for me to realize that social life was back haha. I do encourage everyone to partake in these initiatives.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not really look into this - except of course the Italian courses that were excellent.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely go for the language course and take in as much as you can. I think the world would be a better place if everyone spoke more different languages, instead of just arrogantly assuming english is spoken everywhere.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Bergamo Alta! And Mantova, Lecco and Verona! Vicenza is also beautiful. Visit museums everywhere, as well as palazzi, restaurants etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! The Milanese were very kind, welcoming and actually (quite unexpected for at metropol) patient with my Italian.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Reach out early in the semester/trimester, dont be timid!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Coffee, food, relaxed attitudes, beautiful language that I could listen to all day. Architecture, art.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Start planning early! Reach out to local students as soon as classes begin.
2. Find a local café that serves good coffee, and start going there regularly, and experience true, local Italian coffee-culture.
3. Leave the city and go see some of the fantastic places around Milan. Do one-day trips from 08-20, try local specialties.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I lived with two other students (Danish as well). That was great. We had an emergency situation, where I was very glad to be along friends. I can recommend looking for flatmates.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning Italian. No doubt. And some fun exams.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Time management, and courage to reach out and arrange activities.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
